name: vercel-labs/agent-desktop
description: Computer use CLI for AI agents
readmeExcerpt: agent-desktop Computer use for AI agents: see and operate desktop apps on macOS, Windows, and Linux through the OS accessibility tree. agent-desktop gives an AI agent computer use without screenshots or pixel matching. It reads the accessibility tree of a desktop app and returns it as JSON, with a ref for every element the agent can act on. The agent clicks or types on a ref, reads the UI again to check the result, and repeats. The loop lives in your agent; agent-desktop has no model inside. It ships as a CLI and a C library. Snapshots, clipboard reads, screenshots, command output, and debug artifacts can contain private desktop content. Keep them out of public logs and uploads. Install Bun, Yarn and pnpm can install the same package. It includes native binaries and platform helpers for x64 and ARM64. For direct execution without a JavaScript launcher, download the matching native archive from GitHub Releases and keep its helper beside the executable. On macOS and Linux, Homebrew also works: `brew install agent-desktop`. There is no official Scoop package yet. The repository no longer maintains a custom Homebrew tap or Scoop bucket. Plus, Worktrunk has a bunch of quality-of-life features to simplify working with many parallel changes, including hooks to automate local workflows & copy-on-write build caches. name: JustVugg/colibri
description: A hierarchical inference engine for frontier MoE models: hot experts on the GPU (CUDA, Vulkan), warm ones in RAM, cold ones streamed from NVMe. Written in C, runs on the hardware you already own.
readmeExcerpt: Website · Discord · English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · Italiano · 日本語 · Bahasa Indonesia · Português (Brasil) **Tiny engine, immense model.** colibri runs very large open models on the machine you already have. A mixture-of-experts model of hundreds of billions of parameters uses only a small part of itself for each token, so colibri keeps that part in RAM and reads the rest, the experts, from the disk when the model asks for them. Pure C, one file per model family, no GPU required. Thirteen engines run today. Ten are for language models: **GLM-5.2/5.3** (which also runs **Mistral-Large-4**), **GLM-5.3-Flash**, **Inkling**, **Kimi K3**, **DeepSeek V4 Flash**, **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash**, **MiMo-V2.6 Flash** (and Pro), **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next**, **Qwen3.6** (which also runs Qwen3-Coder, the dense Qwen3.8-27B, **Flint**, **Muse Spark Open** and **LFM3-VL**) and **OLMoE**. One draws pictures: **Qwen-Image-2.1**. Two answer decisions: **Laya** and **GLiNER2.5-Decide**, with a third decision model, **Clef**, on the Qwen3.6 engine. name: p-e-w/heretic
description: Training-free language model modification: Remove censorship, suppress slop, reduce sycophancy, and more
readmeExcerpt: Heretic Training-free language model modification **Remove censorship**, suppress slop, reduce sycophancy, and more. All in an afternoon, on your gaming PC.                     Modify any LLM that you can run on your hardware[^1] [^1]: Heretic supports on-the-fly 4-bit model quantization with bitsandbytes, which can reduce the amount of VRAM required to process a model to the same amount that is used to run a typical quantized version of it, at a slight accuracy cost. Set the `quantization` option to `bnb_4bit` to enable this. Heretic is a unique tool that lets you do what only corporations with access to massive computing power usually do: *Modify,* rather than merely run, language models. It does not perform expensive training; rather, it uses a collection of mathematical techniques to steer behavior based on contrasting example prompts and matching scorers. Heretic can, depending on the configuration: * **Suppress refusals/remove censorship** (this is the default action) * Reduce slop (`config.noslop.toml`) * Reduce humor (`config.nohumor.toml`) * Reduce sycophancy (`config.nosyco.toml`) * Alter emotional
